get.summary: Every configured cluster and its last known state
get.description: The list of clusters comes from configuration overlaid by the metadata store and is always available; each row's summary is a section that can be stale or unavailable on its own.

get.summary: One configured cluster and its last known state
get.description: Answers 404 when no cluster with that id is configured; 400 when the id is malformed.

put.description: Part of the cluster.write flow. This call changes nothing. Answers only after the write has been read back from the store, so a 200 means every replica that has caught up can already see it. A version that does not match answers 409 KUI-CONFIG-VERSION-CONFLICT; a deployment with no metadata store answers 501. The response is the redacted profile and never an echo of the request.

parameters.description: The session's CSRF token (ADR-019). Required on every mutation

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The version being replaced, quoted; "0" to create

400.description: Invalid value for: header X-Kui-Principal, Invalid value for: header X-Csrf-Token, Invalid value for: header If-Match, Invalid value for: body

delete.summary: Remove one cluster from the metadata store
delete.description: Mutation (cluster.delete). This call changes the cluster and cannot be undone. Removes the stored profile and its credentials. A cluster this deployment also declares in its configuration file answers 409: the store record would go and the file would put it straight back, so the refusal names the file instead of pretending to succeed. A deployment with no metadata store answers 501.

parameters.name: X-Csrf-Token
parameters.description: The session's CSRF token (ADR-019). Required on every mutation

get.summary: The cluster's brokers, with rack, controller flag and replica counts
get.description: Read from the cluster snapshot, not from a fresh admin call: the response carries the time it was scraped, and a section status saying whether that time is current.
Read-only in M1: BR-002 ships without edits, which arrive in M5 with read-only mode and audit. A setting the broker marks sensitive has no value and says so.

parameters.name: brokerId
parameters.description: The broker's node id, as the cluster reports it

parameters.name: docs
parameters.description: Ask the broker for each setting's documentation (Kafka 2.6+)

400.description: Invalid value for: header X-Kui-Principal, Invalid value for: path parameter brokerId, Invalid value for: query parameter docs

get.summary: Log directories and their sizes, for one broker or for all of them
get.description: A directory that is offline carries its own error while the rest of the answer is good, which is how Kafka reports a failed disk.

parameters.name: brokerId

400.description: Invalid value for: header X-Kui-Principal, Invalid value for: query parameter brokerId

post.summary: Ask for this cluster to be scraped now
post.description: Answers 202 with the time the request was taken. The snapshot is not new when this returns; the response exists so a button has something truthful to say.

post.summary: Can KUI reach this cluster with these settings?
post.description: Part of the cluster.write flow. This call changes nothing. Opens one bounded connection and describes the cluster, which exercises DNS, TCP, TLS and SASL in one call. It stores nothing. The answer distinguishes 'could not reach it' from 'reached it and it refused our credentials', because those send an operator to two different forms.

get.summary: A cluster's resolved connection settings, for another KUI service
get.description: The ETag is the profile's store version. A caller keeps the last profile it saw and re-fetches with If-None-Match; an unchanged profile answers 304 with no body. This document carries the cluster's credentials, because a consuming service builds a Kafka client from it (ADR-046). It is served on /internal/v1 only, and only to a service principal (`PrincipalKind.System`); /internal/v1 must not be exposed outside the deployment network.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: The ETag the caller already holds; '*' always fetches

get.summary: One event whenever a cluster's profile changes or a cluster is removed
get.description: Named events: 'clusters' carries {id, version, change, at}; 'heartbeat' keeps proxies from closing an idle connection; 'error' carries the standard envelope. A frame carries no profile - a consumer that sees an unfamiliar version fetches it, which keeps credentials off every subscriber's socket and makes a dropped frame cost a fetch rather than a stale client.
Whether the process should be restarted. Never depends on an upstream.
Whether the service can serve requests now, and which checks say otherwise.
What this service can currently do, per cluster.
